event_overview.title: About the 2026 FIFA World Cup
event_overview.subject: FIFA World Cup
event_overview.summary: The FIFA World Cup is FIFA’s flagship men’s national-team football competition, held in four-year cycles and bringing together teams that qualify through their regional confederations. The 2026 edition was staged jointly by Canada, Mexico and the United States and expanded the finals field from 32 to 48 teams, making it the largest edition of the tournament to date.

facts.label: Governing body
facts.value: The competition is organized by the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA), whose statutes govern FIFA competitions and the process for awarding World Cup hosting rights.

facts.label: Origins
facts.value: FIFA approved the launch of the World Cup at its 1928 Congress, and the first tournament was held in Uruguay in 1930 with 13 participating teams.

facts.label: 2026 dates and hosts
facts.value: The 2026 FIFA World Cup ran from June 11 to July 19, 2026, across Canada, Mexico and the United States; it was the first World Cup co-hosted by three countries.

facts.label: Scale and format
facts.value: The 2026 finals featured 48 national teams, 104 matches and 12 groups of four. The top two teams in each group plus the eight best third-placed teams advanced to a round of 32, followed by single-elimination rounds.

facts.label: Host footprint
facts.value: Matches were assigned to 16 host cities: two in Canada, three in Mexico and 11 in the United States.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a late-July and early-August 2026 debate over proposed World Cup investment or equity arrangements and reactions from FIFA and UEFA; it does not aim to document the tournament’s matches, results, or the full history of FIFA governance and commercial operations.
